item.title: Eiheiji Temple: A Working Zen Monastery Deep in the Cedar Forest — Guide
item.description: Eiheiji Temple was founded in 1244 by the monk Dogen, founder of the Soto school of Zen Buddhism, and remains one of the school’s two head temples and an active training monastery today, home to monks who follow a strict daily schedule of meditation, chores and study. The temple’s numerous wooden halls are connected by a network of covered wooden corridors deep within a towering cedar forest, and visitors can walk the same corridors used by resident monks, while a scenic valley nature trail nearby offers a quieter forest walk beyond the temple grounds themselves.
